info.name: Wayfare Flight Booking API
info.description:
Tests every backend endpoint of the Wayfare flight booking app: the browser-facing API, the OAuth2 token-exchange proxy, and the travel-api contract for the future booking-agent/MCP project.

**The endpoint is fully editable** - it's the `baseUrl` collection variable (Variables tab, or use the bundled environments to switch between AWS and local with one click).

### Auth you need to fill in yourself

- `travelApiKey` - the `TRAVEL_API_KEY` value from the server's `.env` on whichever host you're testing. Never commit a real value here; it's left as a placeholder deliberately.
- `thunderIdAccessToken` - a real ThunderID access token. Postman can't easily replicate this app's exact PKCE + CORS-avoiding backend-proxy login flow, so the simplest way to get one: sign in through the actual site in a browser, open devtools console, and run:
  ```js
  JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('tb_session')).accessToken
  ```
  Paste the result into the `thunderIdAccessToken` variable. It expires (see the token's own `exp` claim, typically 1 hour), so you'll need a fresh one periodically.

### Folders

1. **Health** - no auth
2. **Browser-facing API** - the frontend's own routes; auth via `thunderIdAccessToken`
3. **travel-api contract** - for the future MCP project; auth via `travelApiKey`

variable.description: Backend base URL. Edit this (or switch environments) to point at AWS, local dev, or anywhere else this is deployed.
TRAVEL_API_KEY from the target server's .env - guards the travel-api contract routes.
A real ThunderID access token for a signed-in user. See collection description for how to grab one.
ThunderID `sub` of a traveler who has signed in at least once (this is the `admin@example.com` account used during development - replace with any real traveler's sub).
A seeded flight id (id=1 is JFK -> LAX, Wayfare Air WA101).
IATA origin code for search requests.
IATA destination code for search requests.
Optional YYYY-MM-DD filter for search requests. Leave blank to match any date.
Used by the travel-api book_flight request. Run the same request twice with this unchanged to see the 409 duplicate-booking replay behavior; change it to make a genuinely new booking.

item.name: Browser-facing API
item.description: What the frontend itself calls. The three /api/me/* routes require a real ThunderID access token - see the collection description for how to obtain one.

request.description: Requires a real ThunderID access token. Verified server-side against ThunderID's own /oauth2/userinfo endpoint on every call. Returns { profile: {...} } or 401 if the token is invalid/expired.
Requires a real ThunderID access token. Returns { bookings: [...] }.
Requires a real ThunderID access token. 201 + { booking: {...} } on success, 409 if the flight is sold out, 404 if flightId doesn't exist.

Internal route the frontend calls right after a ThunderID redirect - exists because ThunderID's own /oauth2/token endpoint has no CORS support, so the browser can't call it directly. Included here for completeness, but not practical to drive from Postman: the authorization code is single-use and expires within seconds/minutes, and the code_verifier only exists in the browser's sessionStorage from that specific login attempt. The realistic way to get a token for the requests above is the browser-devtools method in the collection description, not this endpoint.

item.name: travel-api contract
item.description: Exact REST contract from the future booking-agent/MCP implementation brief: get_my_profile, list_my_bookings, search_flights, book_flight. All four require the shared TRAVEL_API_KEY bearer token - see the collection description for where to find it.

request.description: traveler_id is the ThunderID `sub`, not an internal database id. Returns { traveler_id, name, email, home_airport, tier, policy_max_fare_usd } or 404.
Returns a bare array: [ { booking_id, flight_id, origin, destination, depart_at, fare_class, price_usd, status } ].
Returns a bare array: [ { flight_id, carrier, origin, destination, depart_at, arrive_at, fare_class, price_usd, fare_rules_text } ].

201 + { booking_id, status, price_usd } on a new booking. Run again UNCHANGED (same idempotencyKey variable) to see 409 + the original booking returned instead of a duplicate. 404 for an unknown traveler/flight, 422 if sold out, 400 if a field is missing.
